images.caption: Figure 1.Overview of CLIP-CC-Bench. Top: dataset construction curates∼\sim90 s movie clips, collects live narration without proper nouns, applies a grammar-only GPT-4o cleanup, and yields the CLIP-CC-Dataset (200 clip–paragraph pairs, 5 h total). Bottom: per-judge evaluation. A candidate paragraphPPfrom one of 17 VLMs (left; sample shown is mPLUG-Owl3 on clip 092) and the reference paragraphGGfrom the dataset (right) are scored by Judgejj, one of five MTEB embedding judges. The judge combines ann×nn{\times}nsentence-level cosine matrix (Fine-Grained Semantic Matching; greedy diagonal best-matches outlined in red) with the paragraph-level cosine (Coarse-Grained Semantic Matching) into a harmonic-meanHM​-​CFj\mathrm{HM\text{-}CF}_{j}. Borda aggregation across the five judges produces the leaderboard over the 17 VLMs.

Figure 2.Distribution of description characteristics in CLIP-CC-Bench. The dataset exhibits substantial variation in both word count and sentence length, reflecting the diverse complexity of video content while maintaining comprehensive paragraph-level descriptions suitable for evaluating long-form video understanding capabilities.
